blocks.html: Kilimanjaro National Park draws travellers who are ready for a challenge. On this page we go through everything you need to know about trekking Mount Kilimanjaro, from the Kilimanjaro itineraries we recommend most to the practical side of getting ready for the adventure of a lifetime.

blocks.orig: Once you’ve made the decision to climb Mount Kilimanjaro, the next step is to choose the best route for you. There are a total of seven main Mount Kilimanjaro routes which lead to the summit. One route begins on the Northern side of the mountain and the remaining six begin on the Southern side. Your Tanzania Trip offers climbing Kilimanjaro itineraries for all the different Kilimanjaro Routes. The main question is which route should you choose?
blocks.html: Once you have decided to climb Mount Kilimanjaro, your next task is picking the route that suits you best. Seven main Mount Kilimanjaro routes lead to the summit in total. One of them starts on the northern side of the mountain; the other six start on the southern side. Your Tanzania Trip offers Kilimanjaro climbing itineraries on every one of these routes. So the big question is: which route is right for you?

blocks.orig: Also known as the “Whiskey Route”, Kilimanjaro’s Machame Route is one the most popular climbing routes in Tanzania. Better yet, this route has a fantastically high success rate. The route has a gradual ascend which gives your body more time to adjust to the altitude. The trail circles around the mountain, offering up spectacular views and a wide variety of landscapes.
blocks.html: Kilimanjaro’s Machame Route, nicknamed the “Whiskey Route”, is one of the most popular climbing routes in Tanzania, and it has an impressively high success rate too. The ascent is gradual, giving your body more time to adapt to the altitude. The trail winds around the mountain, serving up spectacular views and a great variety of landscapes.

blocks.orig: During this route, you will walk through the green rainforest to the amazing Shira Plateau. The last ascent to the crater rim at Stella Point is probably the most challenging part of this route and does require at least a basic level of fitness.
blocks.html: Along this route you walk through green rainforest up to the remarkable Shira Plateau. The final push to the crater rim at Stella Point is probably the toughest section of the route, and it does call for at least a basic level of fitness.

blocks.orig: How long the Machame Route takes is up to you! It can be done in 6 or 7 days and, in our experience, there is a much higher chance of submitting Africa’s largest mountain on a 7-day Kilimanjaro hike!
blocks.html: You decide how long the Machame Route takes! It can be completed in 6 or 7 days, and in our experience the odds of reaching the top of Africa’s largest mountain are far better on a 7-day Kilimanjaro hike!

blocks.orig: PRO: The Machame Route is less expensive than most of the others, due to its shorter route and easy access
blocks.html: PRO: Because the route is shorter and easy to reach, the Machame Route costs less than most of the others

blocks.orig: CON: This route can be quite busy, especially during the peak season
blocks.html: CON: The route can get fairly crowded, particularly in peak season

blocks.orig: This route, nicknamed the “Coca-Cola” route, has a reputation for being one of the easiest paths on the mountain. Though it is certainly the shortest route on the mountain, this does not necessarily mean it is the easiest! As this is a shorter route, your body has less time to acclimatize properly, increasing the chances of fatigue and ultimately decreasing the chances of reaching the summit on this route.
blocks.html: Nicknamed the “Coca-Cola” route, this trail is known as one of the easiest ways up the mountain. It is certainly the shortest route, but that does not automatically make it the easiest! With less time on the mountain, your body has less chance to acclimatise properly, which raises the risk of fatigue and ultimately lowers your chances of making it to the summit on this route.

blocks.orig: Some climbers prefer this route because of the hut accommodation, in contrast to camping in tents as is seen on the majority of other mountain treks. Unfortunately, this also means less privacy! (Plus, there’s nothing like camping out under African skies!). The Marangu Route is the best for those on a budget and is one of the cheapest routes to reach the top of Kilimanjaro.
blocks.html: Some climbers choose this route because you sleep in huts rather than in tents, as you do on most other mountain treks. The flip side is less privacy! (And there is nothing quite like camping beneath African skies!) The Marangu Route is the best option if you are watching your budget, as it is one of the cheapest ways to reach the top of Kilimanjaro.

blocks.orig: PRO: The Marangu Route is one of the cheapest and quickest Mount Kilimanjaro routes. This route also offers hut accommodation in dorm rooms – a benefit for those looking to stay away from camping!
blocks.html: PRO: The Marangu Route is among the cheapest and fastest routes up Mount Kilimanjaro. It also provides hut accommodation in dormitories, a plus for anyone who would rather not camp!

blocks.orig: CON: This route can be quite busy, especially during the peak season. As you will do the same trail for your descent as you did for your ascent, you get to see less of the spectacular scenery!
blocks.html: CON: The route can get fairly crowded, particularly in peak season. Because you descend along the same trail you climbed, you see less of the spectacular scenery!

blocks.orig: The Lemosho Route is a beautiful and unique route, known for its breathtaking views. In contrary to other Mount Kilimanjaro climbing routes, it starts on the western side of Kilimanjaro. Because of this, the Leomosho Route is less crowded with climbers and offers a much more secluded hiking experience.
blocks.html: The Lemosho Route is a beautiful and distinctive route, famous for its breathtaking views. Unlike the other Mount Kilimanjaro climbing routes, it begins on the western flank of Kilimanjaro. As a result, the Leomosho Route sees fewer climbers and gives you a far more secluded hiking experience.

blocks.orig: Better yet, the Lemosho trail is completely unspoiled, making for a breathtakingly beautiful adventure up to the famous Shira Plateau. After a few days, the Lemosho Route joins the Machame Route at Lava Tower. You can do this route in 7 or 8 days, and it does require a decent level of fitness!
blocks.html: What is more, the Lemosho trail is entirely unspoilt, making the climb to the famous Shira Plateau a stunningly beautiful adventure. After a few days the Lemosho Route merges with the Machame Route at Lava Tower. The route takes 7 or 8 days and does demand a reasonable level of fitness!

blocks.orig: CONS: Lemosho is undoubtedly a more expensive route – it’s a long trail and requires extra transport to the other side of the mountain.
blocks.html: CONS: Lemosho is without doubt a pricier route: the trail is long and you need extra transport to reach the far side of the mountain.

blocks.orig: PROS: The price is definitely worth it! The Lemosho route gives climbers plenty of time to acclimatize properly, the views are spectacular and the success rates to reach the summit are high. This is one of the most beautiful and complete routes to climb Kilimanjaro.
blocks.html: PROS: It is money well spent! On the Lemosho Route climbers get plenty of time to acclimatise properly, the views are spectacular and the summit success rates are high. It is one of the most beautiful and complete ways to climb Kilimanjaro.

blocks.html: You can climb Mount Kilimanjaro at any time of year. At Your Tanzania Trip we give expert advice on the best moment to plan your Kilimanjaro trip, based on your personal requirements.

blocks.orig: The two main climbing seasons are the dry months from December to March and from June to October. The warmest months are from December to March. During these months the skies are clearer and there is less chance of snow on the trail. February is the best month since the temperature is high and the chances of rainfall are low. From June to October, the temperatures on the mountain are noticeably colder and the trails are busier.
blocks.html: The two main climbing seasons are the dry months of December to March and June to October. December to March is the warmest period: the skies are clearer and snow on the trail is less likely. February is the best month of all, with high temperatures and a low chance of rain. From June to October it is noticeably colder on the mountain and the trails are busier.

blocks.orig: During the rainy season, it can be wet, slippery and the visibility may be limited. Most climbers avoid these seasons, although some experienced climbers and adventurous travellers prefer to climb at this time. There are certainly some pros: a lack of crowds being a big draw!
blocks.html: In the rainy season conditions can be wet and slippery, and visibility may be poor. Most climbers steer clear of these months, although some experienced climbers and adventurous travellers actually prefer to go then. There are definite upsides, and the absence of crowds is a big one!

blocks.orig: Even though there is a route for every level on Mount Kilimanjaro, it’s important to be able to cope with around 6-7 hours of walking every single day. This can be gruelling, so preparation is always a fantastic idea. During an average climbing day, you will walk 6-7 hours per day. In the months leading up to your trip, head out on long hikes every few weeks, gradually building up your stamina to endure a full weekend hike.
blocks.html: Although Mount Kilimanjaro has a route for every level, you need to be able to handle roughly 6-7 hours of walking every single day. That can be exhausting, so preparing is always a good idea. On a typical climbing day you will be on your feet for 6-7 hours. In the months before your trip, go on long hikes every few weeks, slowly building your stamina until you can manage a full weekend of hiking.

blocks.orig: Other exercises that can help with preparing for your trek include yoga and breathing classes. Stretching out your body and mind makes your muscles stronger and less likely to let you down when you need them most!
blocks.html: Yoga and breathing classes are other useful ways to prepare for your trek. Stretching body and mind makes your muscles stronger and less likely to fail you when you need them most!
